findings.text: Lowered from defect to advisory. `perSentence` and the guard at line 202 are not a dead path under Q4. `DistillInput.wording?: 1 | 2` (src/judge/types.ts:31) is a public contract that allows wording 1 together with candidates, and tests/unit/questions.test.ts:94-105 pins what that combination returns: durable [0,0,0] and no title. The guard also hides no cause (Q9's defect needs that): without it, a version 1 input would read `knowledge_<i>` and `title` answers that were never asked. No production caller sends this combination today, so it stays as a note.
Upheld as advisory (Q3, a name that could be sharper). `distillQuestionsV1` matches version 1 only when there are no candidates.

Upheld as advisory. The reviewer says this is a correctness gap against AC-1, not a failure of a code-quality rubric question. `withoutSentences` has no `g` flag, so the second copy of a repeated noise sentence stays in `finalText`. The fix belongs to the noise filter and its tests.
Upheld as advisory (Q2). The reviewer calls it boilerplate-level duplication: `toldInSession` and `unfilteredTexts` run twice for one turn in a proof script.
Upheld as advisory (Q9). The bare `catch {}` in `readingOf` counts a coding error as a TypeSafe failure. It is in an offline proof script, off the hook path.
Upheld as advisory (Q6). The comment is one line over 100 characters, a style difference from its neighbours.
Debt, outside the change. `hasDurable` hard-codes 0.5 while KNOWLEDGE_THRESHOLD is 0.45. The diff did not write this line.

Dropped as a defect, kept as advisory. The finding claims that no test fails when the REPORT_DISCOUNT is removed. The probe disproves it: probes/report-discount-removed.txt shows that with `worth -= 0;` the test 'heuristic judge, version 2: records of a session > a report with a cue word in it is not worth saving when every sentence is a report' fails (61 pass, 1 fail). AC-5's discount therefore has a test that fails when it is reverted (Q1 answered). The reviewer worked out its scores by hand and ran nothing.

Upheld as defect (Q1, AC-11 behavior: 'the proof script measures the metrics of the spec'). The success test checks only the 'Memories stored' cell (line 231). The failure test checks only 'n/a' cells and a zero (lines 244-248). No test checks a computed value of 'Title is knowledge', 'Lost, of knowledge and mixed turns', 'Stored from record or fragment', 'Title-only' or the v1 and heuristic columns. The predicates `titleIsKnowledge`, `lost` and `records` (scripts/proof/quality.ts) could be inverted and every test would still pass. The stand-in answers deterministically and the labels quote fixed candidates, so those values can be checked.

Upheld as advisory. The fixture writes no injections, so the proof test never shows the bound to the turn's end. That bound is covered through the shared `toldInSession` by tests/integration/distill.test.ts:973-991. The 'Sentences dropped per pattern' line is not checked.

Upheld as advisory. The replaying stand-in does not tie the recording to the question wording. A missing `knowledge_<i>` key would still be caught, and the wording is spot-checked in tests/unit/questions.test.ts.
Upheld as advisory, hardening only. The proof's outputs depend on quality.sh's `umask 077` when the script is run directly. The documented route is the wrapper.
Upheld as advisory. `WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_TYPESAFE_URL` is honoured only outside the wrapper (quality.sh unsets WIZARDINGCODE_*). The live drain behaves the same way, and the caller owns the key.

Upheld as advisory. In the live drain, filter drops are not recorded, so a filter-emptied skip looks the same as a judge rejection. The spec names this risk (design section 12), and turn text stays for 90 days, so the effect can be seen and undone.
Upheld as advisory. Recovering version 2's lost turns depends on D-1 within compact's 90-day window. The spec states that dependency. No owner or date is named.
Upheld as advisory. The cost of the first full `history import` under version 2 is measured per turn but never estimated for the whole run. The run is bounded and resumable.
Lowered to advisory as debt. This file is not in the diff. The interaction with replace-imports is undone by `history restore-imports`.

Upheld as advisory, not a defect. The rollback is stated: spec.md:33 says rollback is a release and the rows stay valid through `judge_version`. No dependency goes unnamed. The reviewer shows that mixed v1 and v2 binaries on one store are harmless. Only the release steps are not listed.
Debt, outside the change. Supersession through `consolidate` existed before this change.
Upheld as advisory (rubric Q5). The level 3 importance wording departs from the Design's wording and crosses no boundary. Either align the wording or record the change in the spec or ADR 0023.
Debt, outside the change. The heuristic's 0.5 durable cut (lines 148 and 188) differs from KNOWLEDGE_THRESHOLD 0.45. These lines are unchanged context.
Upheld as advisory (Q5, personal data). The work-dir copy of the store and the samples are kept with no stated retention or erasure step. They are protected by umask 077 and the never-commit note.
Upheld as advisory. `toldInSession` scans `injections` because the only index is partial. The scan predates the change and the new predicate does not make it worse.
Upheld as advisory. The correlated NOT EXISTS on `memories` has no index on those columns. It runs once on the copy, off any hook path.
Debt, outside the change. `injections` has no plain index on `session_id`.
